description: Pilot single-encrypt-call wall-clock timing measured before sizing the NPCR/UACI (Experiment E) and key-sensitivity (Experiment F) trial matrices, per the mandatory pilot requirement. Backend = numpy unless noted. Measured with isc_cipher._testing.encrypt_bytes_with_nonce_TEST_ONLY and isc_cipher.cipher.encrypt_bytes, fixed/random key+nonce, os.urandom plaintext.

fitted_model_numpy_backend.note: fixed cost dominated by 256-lane x 1024-iteration burn-in (independent of n); marginal cost dominated by the Fisher-Yates permutation-construction loop over n Lemire draws, which is inherently sequential regardless of numpy/reference backend -- this is why numpy and reference backend costs converge at larger n (compare 256x256x1: 4.07s numpy vs 4.11s reference).

decision_npcr_uaci.rationale: Keeping full position x image-type sweeps only at the two cheap sizes (64, 128) and reducing the 256x256 sweep to positions-only with one image type keeps the whole experiment under ~90s instead of the >300s a full 3-size x 3-type x 3-position x 2-profile matrix would cost; this is the 'meaningful trials, not hundreds of redundant runs' tradeoff the user asked for.

decision_key_sensitivity.bit_positions_full_sweep: 16 positions (every 16th of 256 key bits), sizes 64 and 128
decision_key_sensitivity.rationale: 256-bit exhaustive key-bit sweep (256 positions) at even one image size would cost ~256*2*1.4s=~717s just at 64x64 alone, and far more at larger sizes; sampling every 16th/32nd bit position gives coverage across all 32 key bytes without that cost, consistent with the spec's own instruction to test 'a reasonable number of key-bit positions', not an exhaustive sweep.
